correctness.rationale: The local algebra has basis 1 and r truncated power branches; arbitrary augmentation-preserving endomorphisms correspond to independent output-branch annihilating tuples. Leading coefficients give fg=0 iff v(f)+v(g)>=d+1 over every field. The coordinatewise-minimal permitted valuations are precisely the displayed incomparable vectors (a,d+1-a,...), plus the all-half vector in even truncation length. They yield all maximal linear irreducible components of the reduced variety. Their dimension formula gives equidimensionality iff r=2 or d=2. A disjoint split into all-high tuples and a unique smaller-valued tuple gives the point count. Literal multiplication and tangent-matrix rank were independently enumerated in verify.py, including a boundary r=3,d=3 test.

originality.rationale: The claim classifies the noninvertible endomorphism variety and its coordinate-linear irreducible components for every branch number and truncation order, identifies its non-equidimensionality boundary and gives total finite-field endomorphism counts. The closest published result for the identical algebra establishes its automorphism group but neither treats the entire endomorphism variety nor implies its other components, component dimensions or all endomorphism counts. A prior result on augmentation-preserving endomorphisms of a truncated two-variable complete intersection treats power-zero constraints, not cross-branch pairwise annihilation. No searched record contained a stronger theorem entailing the stated claim. A possible differently titled treatment of multi-branch zero-product tuples remains a residual priority risk.

value.rationale: The object is the intrinsic parameter space of self-maps of a natural family of zero-dimensional coordinate-cross singularities, built as fiber products of truncated lines. The theorem simultaneously determines all geometrically irreducible components, their dimensions, the exact equidimensionality boundary, the anomalous location of automorphisms in lower-dimensional components for r,d>=3, and the total point count over every finite field. These invariants are not implied by the known automorphism group and are useful for distinguishing the geometry of all self-maps from that of the invertible stratum. The arbitrary-field structural proof and all-q finite census are substantially beyond one finite experiment or parameter substitution.
